Fit a Lorentz Hyperbolic Weighted Regression Model

Source: R/fit.R
lhwr.Rd

Estimate location-varying Gaussian or binomial regression coefficients for observations located on the Lorentz hyperboloid. At each focal point, the function fits an unpenalized weighted linear or logistic regression using kernel weights derived from either intrinsic Lorentz distances or tangent-space distances.

Usage

lhwr(
  formula,
  data,
  Z,
  bw,
  kernel = hgwr_kernel_names(),
  adaptive = TRUE,
  bandwidth_type = c("knn", "volume"),
  geometry = c("lorentz", "tangent"),
  pilot_k = NULL,
  tangent_ref = NULL,
  dMat = NULL,
  engine = c("dense", "knn"),
  n_threads = 1L,
  diagnostics = c("full", "aicc", "none"),
  f_tests = FALSE,
  family = c("gaussian", "binomial"),
  control = stats::glm.control(maxit = 100L)
)

Arguments

formula

Model formula of the form response ~ predictors.

data

Data frame containing the response and predictor variables used in formula.

Z

Numeric n x 3 matrix of Lorentz hyperboloid coordinates. Row i gives the location of observation i and must satisfy <z_i,z_i>_L = -1 with positive time coordinate.

bw

Bandwidth used for local weighting. If adaptive = TRUE, a scalar is interpreted as a neighbor count and converted to a separate radius at each focal location. If adaptive = FALSE, a scalar is interpreted as a fixed radius, or as a fixed hyperbolic volume when bandwidth_type = "volume". A numeric vector of length n may be used to supply one radius per location directly.

kernel

Kernel used to convert distances into local weights. Available choices are "bisquare", "gaussian", "exponential", "tricube", and "boxcar".

adaptive

Logical. If TRUE, scalar bw is treated as a neighbor count. If FALSE, scalar bw is treated as a fixed distance or volume.

bandwidth_type

Bandwidth scale. "knn" uses nearest-neighbor radii. "volume" uses hyperbolic ball volumes and is available only for geometry = "lorentz".

geometry

Distance geometry used to build kernel weights. "lorentz" uses intrinsic hyperbolic distances on the Lorentz hyperboloid. "tangent" maps locations to one tangent plane by the Lorentz logarithmic map and uses the positive-definite Lorentz metric induced on that tangent plane. Equivalently, these distances can be represented as Euclidean distances in a Lorentz-orthonormal tangent basis.

pilot_k

Pilot neighbor count used to estimate local point density for adaptive volume bandwidths. Ignored unless adaptive = TRUE and bandwidth_type = "volume".

tangent_ref

Optional reference point for geometry = "tangent". If omitted, the normalized extrinsic Lorentz mean is used.

dMat

Optional precomputed n x n distance matrix. If supplied, it is used directly instead of computing a distance matrix from Z.

engine

Computational engine. "dense" builds or uses a full distance matrix. "knn" uses exact Lorentz nearest-neighbor lists and avoids storing the full distance matrix; it is available for adaptive Lorentz kNN fits with compact kernels.

n_threads

Number of OpenMP threads used by engine = "knn" when OpenMP is available. The default 1 preserves serial execution.

diagnostics

Diagnostic detail level. "full" returns the traditional diagnostic table, local standard errors, t-values, and local R-squared values when available. "aicc" computes hat-matrix diagnostics for AICc but skips local standard-error and local R-squared columns in the output table. "none" skips hat-matrix diagnostics and returns only fitted values, residuals, local coefficients, RSS, and global R-squared.

f_tests

Logical. If TRUE, compute LHWR diagnostic F-tests after model fitting. The default FALSE avoids the additional smoother reconstruction cost, which can be substantial for large data sets. Diagnostic F-tests are available only for Gaussian LHWR.

family

Response family. "gaussian" fits local weighted least-squares regressions and "binomial" fits local weighted logistic regressions. The default preserves the original Gaussian LHWR behavior.

control

Iteration controls for binomial LHWR, created by stats::glm.control(). epsilon, maxit, and trace are used by the native local IRLS solver. Ignored for Gaussian LHWR.

Value

An object of class "lhwr", a list containing model arguments, diagnostic summaries, the global linear model fit, local coefficient table SDF, coefficient names, local coefficient matrix beta_hat, fitted values, residuals, distance matrix, selected geometry label, effective bandwidth vector, hat-matrix diagonal, local condition numbers, local effective sample sizes, local counts of positive kernel weights, timing information, family-specific convergence information, and the original function call. For binomial models, fitted values are response probabilities and residuals are response residuals y - p.

Details

Standard errors, local test statistics, and fitted-model diagnostics are conditional on the supplied Z matrix and the fitted neighborhood system. If Z is estimated from data, these quantities do not propagate first-stage representation uncertainty. They also do not include uncertainty from data-driven bandwidth selection.

Examples

set.seed(20260615)
n <- 120
H <- simulate_H2(n, r_max = 5, uniform_area = TRUE)
Z <- H$Z
D <- hyperbolic_distance_matrix(Z, check = FALSE)

true_k <- 25
h <- apply(D, 1, function(d) sort(d[d > 0])[true_k])
centers <- round(seq(10, n - 10, length.out = 5))
Phi <- sapply(centers, function(j) {
  hgwr_kernel(D[, j], h[j], kernel = "bisquare")
})

beta0 <- 0.4 + 2 * (1.45 * Phi[, 1] - 1.25 * Phi[, 4])
beta1 <- 1.0 + 2 * (1.65 * Phi[, 2] - 1.20 * Phi[, 5])
beta2 <- -0.8 + 2 * (1.55 * Phi[, 3] - 1.10 * Phi[, 4])

x1 <- as.numeric(scale(rnorm(n)))
x2 <- as.numeric(scale(rnorm(n)))
eta <- beta0 + beta1 * x1 + beta2 * x2
y <- eta + rnorm(n, sd = sqrt(var(eta) / 8))
dat <- data.frame(y = y, x1 = x1, x2 = x2)

bw <- bw.lhwr(
  y ~ x1 + x2,
  data = dat,
  Z = Z,
  approach = "CV",
  adaptive = TRUE,
  geometry = "lorentz",
  bw_grid = seq(10, 80, by = 5)
)

fit <- lhwr(
  y ~ x1 + x2,
  data = dat,
  Z = Z,
  bw = bw$bw,
  adaptive = TRUE,
  geometry = "lorentz"
)
fit
summary(fit)
head(fit$SDF)

beta_true <- cbind(Intercept = beta0, x1 = beta1, x2 = beta2)
sqrt(mean(rowSums((fit$beta_hat - beta_true)^2)))

fit_tangent <- lhwr(
  y ~ x1 + x2,
  data = dat,
  Z = Z,
  bw = bw$bw,
  adaptive = TRUE,
  geometry = "tangent"
)
fit_tangent$geometry

probability <- plogis(-0.4 + 1.1 * x1 - 0.7 * x2)
dat$event <- rbinom(n, 1, probability)
fit_binomial <- lhwr(
  event ~ x1 + x2,
  data = dat,
  Z = Z,
  bw = 40,
  family = "binomial",
  diagnostics = "full"
)
head(fitted(fit_binomial))
